Handle edge case: action_id not found in side_effects (old journal format) - show warning.

subtasks.title: Implement apply_fix + revert_fix with journal recording
subtasks.description: Build apply_fix to call rule's apply_fix() with state guard, record journal entry. Build revert_fix to load journal entry, check state drift, call rule's revert_fix()
subtasks.details:
apply_fix: 1. Extract $_POST['sub_id'], $_POST['rule_id']. 2. Load sub + rule (same as preview). 3. State guard: compute hash of sub's tracked fields (use $rule->tracked_fields()), compare to $_POST['expected_state_hash'] sent from frontend. If mismatch, throw Exception 'Subscription state changed since preview. Refresh and try again.' 4. Call $result = $rule->apply_fix($sub), returns ['success' => bool, 'changes' => array]. 5. Record journal entry: insert into dr_subs_fix_journal (sub_id, rule_id, batch_id=null, before_state=json_encode(tracked fields), after_state=json_encode(new state), applied_at=current_time('mysql'), reverted_at=null). Get insert ID. 6. Return wp_send_json_success(['entry_id' => $wpdb->insert_id, 'message' => 'Fix applied'])

revert_fix: 1. Extract $_POST['entry_id']. 2. Load journal entry: $wpdb->get_row('SELECT * FROM dr_subs_fix_journal WHERE entry_id = %d', $entry_id). 3. Check if already reverted: if reverted_at != null, return error 'Already reverted'. 4. Load sub + rule from entry. 5. State drift check: compare current sub state to entry's after_state. If mismatch, add warnings array to response. 6. Call $rule->revert_fix($entry), pass journal entry object. 7. Update journal: SET reverted_at = current_time('mysql'). 8. Return wp_send_json_success(['message' => 'Fix reverted', 'warnings' => $warnings])

subtasks.title: Implement run_scan, cancel_scan, save_settings handlers
subtasks.description: Build run_scan to trigger async scanner with transient lock, cancel_scan to set cancellation flag, save_settings to validate and persist dr_subs_settings option
subtasks.details:
run_scan: 1. Check transient lock: if get_transient('dr_subs_scan_running') !== false, return error 'Scan already running'. 2. Set transient: set_transient('dr_subs_scan_running', time(), 600) (10min TTL). 3. Trigger async scan: wp_schedule_single_event(time(), 'dr_subs_run_health_scan') (immediate execution). Scanner hook registered elsewhere, calls DR_Subs_Health_Scanner::run(). 4. Return wp_send_json_success(['message' => 'Scan started'])

cancel_scan: 1. Set cancellation flag: set_transient('dr_subs_scan_cancel', true, 300) (5min TTL). Scanner checks this between batches, exits early if true. 2. Delete running lock: delete_transient('dr_subs_scan_running'). 3. Return wp_send_json_success(['message' => 'Scan cancelled'])

save_settings: 1. Extract $_POST['settings'] array. 2. Validate: alerts_enabled (bool via rest_sanitize_boolean), alert_email (sanitize_email + is_email()), journal_retention_days (absint, range 30-365 or -1 for unlimited), telemetry_enabled (bool). Throw Exception on invalid values. 3. Merge with existing: $current = get_option('dr_subs_settings', []), $new = array_merge($current, $validated). 4. update_option('dr_subs_settings', $new). 5. Return wp_send_json_success(['message' => 'Settings saved'])

subtasks.title: Create AJAX handler wp_ajax_dr_subs_bulk_fix

subtasks.details: In includes/class-ajax-handler.php constructor, add: add_action('wp_ajax_dr_subs_bulk_fix', array($this, 'bulk_fix_subscriptions')). tasks.title: Translations: Generate POT and translate to 20 locales
tasks.description: Create translation workflow using WP-CLI and Potomatic for 20 major languages
tasks.details:
1. Create scripts/translate.sh:
   - wp i18n make-pot . languages/doctor-subs.pot --slug=doctor-subs --domain=doctor-subs --include=doctor-subs.php,includes,admin
   - potomatic -l fr_FR,es_ES,de_DE,it_IT,pt_BR,pt_PT,nl_NL,pl_PL,ru_RU,ja,zh_CN,zh_TW,ko_KR,ar,tr_TR,sv_SE,nb_NO,da_DK,fi,cs_CZ -p languages/doctor-subs.pot -o languages/ --po-file-prefix doctor-subs-
   - wp i18n make-mo languages/
   - wp i18n make-json languages/ --no-purge
2. Create config/dictionaries/dictionary.json: {"noTranslate": ["Doctor Subs", "WooCommerce", "WordPress", "Stripe", "Action Scheduler", "PayPal", "Subscription"]}
3. Configure Potomatic to use OPENAI_API_KEY or GEMINI_API_KEY from env
4. Run --dry-run first to estimate cost
5. Generate .po files, commit to git (source of truth)
6. Compile .mo + .json (add to .gitignore, generated on build)
7. Load text domain in DR_Subs_Plugin::__construct() via load_plugin_textdomain()
8. Manual QA: review fr_FR, es_ES, de_DE, it_IT, pt_BR .po files for brand term preservation
tasks.testStrategy: Test POT generation: verify all strings from PHP templates + admin.js extracted. Test Potomatic: run on 2 test locales (fr_FR, es_ES), verify brand terms NOT translated. Test MO compilation: verify .mo files loadable. Test JS translations: verify admin.js strings have .json files. Load site in fr_FR locale, verify dashboard shows French strings.
